provider.name: GRIN Taxonomy
provider.organization_type: plant taxonomy, nomenclature, economic botany, distribution, common-name, bibliography, and germplasm-support information system
provider.description: GRIN Taxonomy is the taxonomic and nomenclatural component of the USDA Agricultural Research Service Germplasm Resources Information Network. It supports the U.S. National Plant Germplasm System with accepted plant names, synonyms, authorship, classification, common names, geographic distributions, economic uses, references, and persistent taxonomic identifiers.

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting GRIN Taxonomy documentation, classification, nomenclature, identifiers, distributions, common names, economic uses, references, reports, APIs, GRIN-Global platform documentation, licensing, citation, and institutional context.
purpose.authoritative_notice: USDA ARS, NPGS, GRIN Taxonomy, GRIN-Global, cited nomenclatural sources, and applicable nomenclatural codes remain authoritative for taxon records, identifiers, classifications, names, references, rights, versions, and contact information.

notes: Verify whether GRIN Taxonomy exposes a supported public API or only web queries and reports.
Distinguish USDA NPGS production services from generic GRIN-Global platform services.

Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
GRIN Taxonomy and GRIN-Global routes may be case-sensitive, redirected, renamed, or generated dynamically; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every taxon, common name, reference, distribution record, germplasm accession, or query result when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store USDA, GRIN-Global, or curator credentials, API keys, cookies, OAuth tokens, or session identifiers in this JSON file.
Taxonomic facts, nomenclatural content, references, common names, distributions, economic uses, downloads, APIs, and software may carry different rights.
